title: For a sheaf the map to the plus construction is an isomorphism
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf of sets on $\mathcal C$, and let $\theta:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G^+$ be the canonical map to its plus construction [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction]. Then $\theta_U:\mathcal G(U)\to\mathcal G^+(U)$ is bijective for every object $U$, i.e. $\theta$ is an isomorphism of presheaves; in particular $\mathcal G^+$ is a sheaf.

source.place: Sites, Theorem 00WB (theorem-plus), part (3) (item-plus-iso, tag 00WE), with its proof

proof.text: *The sheaf condition identifies $\mathcal G(U)$ with every $H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)$.* Let $\mathcal U=\{\pi_i:U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ be a covering. By [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction](a), $H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)\subset\prod_i\mathcal G(U_i)$ is the set of families $(s_i)$ with $s_i|_{U_i\times_UU_j}=s_j|_{U_i\times_UU_j}$ for all $i,j$, i.e. exactly the equalizer of the two maps $\prod_i\mathcal G(U_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\mathcal G(U_i\times_UU_j)$ given by the two projections, and the canonical map is $c_{\mathcal U}:a\mapsto(a|_{U_i})_i$. Since $\mathcal G$ is a sheaf [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1), $\mathcal G(U)\to\prod_i\mathcal G(U_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\mathcal G(U_i\times_UU_j)$ is an equalizer diagram of sets, which says precisely that $c_{\mathcal U}:\mathcal G(U)\to H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)$ is bijective: injective (two sections with the same restrictions to all $U_i$ are equal) and surjective (every compatible family $(s_i)$ is $(a|_{U_i})_i$ for some $a\in\mathcal G(U)$, unique by injectivity). This is the sentence of the source: 'the sheaf property says exactly that every map $\mathcal F\to H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ is bijective'.

source.place: Sites, Theorem 00WB (theorem-plus), proof of part (3) (item-plus-iso, tag 00WE), with the definitions of H^0 and F^+ in Section 00W1 before Lemma 00W4

proof.text: *$\theta_U$ is injective.* Let $a,b\in\mathcal G(U)$ with $\theta_U(a)=\theta_U(b)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction-presheaf](2) (its 'in particular' for $\theta_U$, applied to the presheaf $\mathcal G$) there is a covering $\mathcal V=\{V_k\to U\}_{k\in K}$ with $a|_{V_k}=b|_{V_k}$ for all $k$, i.e. $c_{\mathcal V}(a)=c_{\mathcal V}(b)$. By Step 1, $c_{\mathcal V}$ is injective, so $a=b$.

source.place: Sites, Theorem 00WB (theorem-plus), proof of part (3) (item-plus-iso, tag 00WE), with the definitions of H^0 and F^+ in Section 00W1 before Lemma 00W4

proof.text: *$\theta_U$ is surjective.* Let $x\in\mathcal G^+(U)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction-presheaf](1), $x=[\mathcal U,s]$ for a covering $\mathcal U=\{\pi_i:U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ of $U$ and some $s=(s_i)\in H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)$. By Step 1 there is $a\in\mathcal G(U)$ with $s=c_{\mathcal U}(a)=(\mathcal G(\pi_i)a)_i$. Let $\{\mathrm{id}_U\}$ be the trivial covering (index set a point $*$), an object of $\mathcal J_U$ [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction](c). The triple $f=(\chi,\alpha,(f_i))=(\mathrm{id}_U,\ I\to\{*\},\ (\pi_i)_{i\in I})$ is a morphism of coverings $\mathcal U\to\{\mathrm{id}_U\}$ over $\mathrm{id}_U$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction](b): the required identity $\mathrm{id}_U\circ f_i=\chi\circ\pi_i$ reads $\pi_i=\pi_i$. It is a morphism of $\mathcal J_U$, and with $H^0(\{\mathrm{id}_U\},\mathcal G)=\mathcal G(U)$ (the identification used in the definition of $\theta_U$) the induced map is $(f^*a)_i=\mathcal G(f_i)(a)=\mathcal G(\pi_i)(a)=a|_{U_i}$, i.e. $f^*a=s$. Since the classes $[-,-]$ form the colimit cocone of the functor $H^0(-,\mathcal G)$ on $\mathcal J_U^{opp}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction](c) (for a morphism $f:\mathcal U\to\mathcal U'$ in $\mathcal J_U$ and $t\in H^0(\mathcal U',\mathcal G)$ one has $[\mathcal U,f^*t]=[\mathcal U',t]$), we get $x=[\mathcal U,s]=[\mathcal U,f^*a]=[\{\mathrm{id}_U\},a]=\theta_U(a)$, the last equality being the definition of $\theta_U$.

source.place: Sites, Theorem 00WB (theorem-plus), proof of part (3) (item-plus-iso, tag 00WE), with the definitions of H^0 and F^+ in Section 00W1 before Lemma 00W4

proof.text: *$\theta$ is an isomorphism of presheaves and $\mathcal G^+$ is a sheaf.* By [lem-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction-presheaf](4), $\mathcal G^+$ is a presheaf and $\theta$ a morphism of presheaves: $\theta_V\circ\mathcal G(h)=\mathcal G^+(h)\circ\theta_U$ for every $h:V\to U$. By Steps 2 and 3 every $\theta_U$ is bijective; then $\theta_V^{-1}\circ\mathcal G^+(h)=\theta_V^{-1}\circ\mathcal G^+(h)\circ\theta_U\circ\theta_U^{-1}=\theta_V^{-1}\circ\theta_V\circ\mathcal G(h)\circ\theta_U^{-1}=\mathcal G(h)\circ\theta_U^{-1}$, so $(\theta_U^{-1})_U$ is a morphism of presheaves inverse to $\theta$. For a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$, the bijections $\theta_U$, $\prod_i\theta_{U_i}$, $\prod_{i,j}\theta_{U_i\times_UU_j}$ commute, by naturality of $\theta$ for the morphisms $U_i\to U$ and the two projections $U_i\times_UU_j\to U_i,U_j$, with the maps of the diagrams $\mathcal G(U)\to\prod_i\mathcal G(U_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\mathcal G(U_i\times_UU_j)$ and $\mathcal G^+(U)\to\prod_i\mathcal G^+(U_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\mathcal G^+(U_i\times_UU_j)$; a diagram of sets isomorphic to an equalizer diagram is an equalizer diagram, so $\mathcal G^+$ satisfies the sheaf condition of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1).

split_report.summary: Split following the proof of Stacks Sites Theorem 00WB(3) (tag 00WE), which says only that the sheaf property makes every G(U) -> H^0(U_cov,G) bijective. Written out in 4 steps: (1) the sheaf condition is exactly bijectivity of the canonical map to H^0 of every covering (elementary, from the definitions); (2) injectivity of theta_U from clause (2) of lem-weil-pbc-site-plus-construction-presheaf and separatedness; (3) surjectivity from clause (1) of that node, Step 1, and the morphism of coverings (id_U, I->{*}, (pi_i)) from U_cov to the trivial covering, with the colimit cocone property of the definition; (4) the inverse of theta is natural (clause (4) of the presheaf node) and the sheaf condition transports along the isomorphism, giving the 'in particular G^+ is a sheaf' used by the citer lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-plus-theorem. Statement and stmt_deps kept. No new nodes.
